dedup_rule: DOI, else PMID, else normalised title (ASCII-folded, alphanumeric only)
doi_rule: a PubMed record's DOI is read from PubmedData/ArticleIdList, else from the article's ELocationID; never from its reference list

corrections.what: Until this date the DOI was the last ArticleId of type doi anywhere in the record, which includes the cited-reference list: 2719 PubMed records were keyed by a reference's DOI and distinct records merged as duplicates (10059 unique, 1303 removed before the correction).
corrections.effect: rebuilt with the record's own DOI; the counts in this file changed

corrections.what: The three Scopus queries of amendment AM-7 were added to the pool. Scopus had been a declared gap since 2026-09-13 because its API needs a key; the investigator ran the queries in the institutional web interface.
corrections.effect: the pool grew and the counts in this file changed; every record that entered through Scopus alone is unscreened until a dated screening round says otherwise

title_key_risk: a record with no DOI and no PMID is keyed by its normalised title, which merges the same work across databases and fails to merge it when a subtitle differs. The count above is how many records that applies to.

same_normalised_title_on_several_records.defect: these are the same work entered twice, not two works with one title, in every case inspected. The key order is DOI, then PMID, then normalised title, so a work that PubMed gives a DOI for and Scopus does not is keyed two different ways and never merged.
same_normalised_title_on_several_records.known_consequence: the unique record count above is an overcount by at most the difference between records_involved and groups, the duplicates are ranked twice by the prioritiser, and one work is in the priority stratum twice and was screened in twice, once in each round.
same_normalised_title_on_several_records.not_fixed_here: merging on normalised title needs a guard against short and generic titles, and it would move the strata, the samples drawn from them and the screening judgements made over those samples. It is a correction of its own.
